articles.title: Sydney Sweeney breaks silence on split from fiancé after 3-year engagement
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney, known for her role in "Euphoria," ends her engagement to Jonathan Davino as she focuses on self-discovery and launches a unique product.
articles.body: After months of speculation, Sydney Sweeney is finally setting the record straight. The 26-year-old actress confirmed she has called off her engagement to longtime partner Jonathan Davino, 41. When asked if she was still planning a wedding, she simply replied "No" during an interview with The Times UK. Sweeney said "yes" when asked if she’s single. SYDNEY SWEENEY DELETES KISSING INSTAGRAM PHOTO WITH FIANCÉ AS BREAKUP RUMORS SWIRL "I’m learning a lot about myself, spending more time with my friends. And I’m loving it," she said. Representatives for Sweeney did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The split marked the end of a relationship that began in 2018. Sweeney stopped wearing her engagement ring in February after the couple got engaged in 2022. Davino worked alongside Sweeney and co-produced the film "Anyone But You." Rumors swirled that Sweeney and her co-star Glen Powell were dating around the time they filmed their rom-com. In March, the "Euphoria" star seemingly deleted a once "favorite" memory from her social media with Davino. While rumors of their breakup continued to circulate online at the time, fans noticed a small detail missing from Sweeney’s Instagram account. In a celebratory New Year's post shared Jan. 2, Sweeney included a photo of her and Davino kissing, with friends laughing and smiling in the background. LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS However, the photo was no longer part of the carousel, which included a caption that said, "The last few days of 2024 will forever be some of my favorite." Last year, Sweeney opened up about her decision to be with a man 14 years older. "I’m a very successful, independent woman who’s worked really hard," Sweeney told Glamour magazine in October. "I’ve accomplished and bought everything myself, and I provide for myself and my family." SYDNEY SWEENEY SLAMS FINANCIALLY FUELED PRECONCEIVED NOTIONS ABOUT HER RELATIONSHIP WITH 40-YEAR-OLD FIANCÉ "I would love to set the record straight," she added. "You can be in a healthy relationship with someone and also be very successful without needing the man. We’re teammates. We’re in it together. And we want to see each other succeed." The news of Sweeney’s split comes after she announced she is selling her used bathwater to her fans. "You kept asking about my bathwater after the Dr. Squatch ad… so we kept it," she wrote in an Instagram post. "Introducing Sydney’s Bathwater Bliss! A very real, very limited-edition soap made with my actual bathwater." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER In 2024, the "Euphoria" star teamed up with Dr. Squatch Natural Body Wash, and her advertisement caption on social media said, "For my dirty little boys out there."Sweeney was taking a bubble bath in the ad, and comments poured in about her bathwater. "How much for the water?" one fan wrote. Other comments sparked interest in even wanting to taste her bathwater. "The White Lotus" star told GQ she "definitely was not aware" of the erotic implications of bathtub water "until I started seeing it in my own comments." CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP When asked if she was surprised about the particular request for her bathwater, she replied it was a "really fun, full-circle moment.""Fans always joke about wanting my bath water. … I was like, ‘This is just such a cool way to have a conversation with the audience and give them what they want.’ But then also hopefully encourage them to take care of themselves in a healthy way." Fox News Digital's Christina Dugan Ramirez contributed to this report.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney stays quiet on American Eagle campaign, unapologetic about bathwater soap
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney "won't comment" on American Eagle jeans campaign uproar, according to the Wall Street Journal, which just published a new interview with the star.
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney is defending her controversial bathwater soap, but remaining mum about her American Eagle jeans campaign. According to the Wall Street Journal, which just published a new interview with Sweeney, the actress "won't comment" on the uproar over the jeans ad. However, she did tell the magazine during their sit-down, which took place earlier this summer, that she keeps an eye on what’s being said about her on social media, but she doesn’t let it bother her. "I think it’s important to have a finger on the pulse of what people are saying, because everything is a conversation with the audience," she told the Journal in the interview published this week. SYDNEY SWEENEY ROCKS BLUE JEANS AS SHE BREAKS SOCIAL MEDIA SILENCE AFTER AMERICAN EAGLE AD CONTROVERSY The ad in question involved Sweeney in denim for American Eagle, playing on the homophones "jeans" and "genes" that sparked accusations of eugenics. The ad is part of the company’s "Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans" campaign. In the ad that sparked backlash, Sweeney tells the viewer that genes are "passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair color, personality, and even eye color." "My jeans are blue," she finishes after the camera has swept up her recumbent body and closes in on her eyes. The ad has since been removed from the company’s social media pages. American Eagle released a statement on its social media earlier this month, saying, "‘Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans’ is and always was about the jeans. Her jeans. Her story. We’ll continue to celebrate how everyone wears their AE jeans with confidence, their way. Great jeans look good on everyone." A rep for Sweeney did not respond to Fox News Digital's previous requests for comment on the backlash. SYDNEY SWEENEY'S BROTHER MAKES CHEEKY 'GOOD JEANS' JOKE AFTER HIS AIR FORCE PROMOTION Sweeney also stirred the tub water recently when she made several suggestive ads for Dr. Squatch, a line of natural bath products for men, and collaborated on a limited line of soap made from her own used bathwater. Sydney’s Bathwater Bliss sold out immediately. "I think it’s important to have a finger on the pulse of what people are saying, because everything is a conversation with the audience." "It was mainly the girls making comments about it, which I thought was really interesting," she told the Journal. "They all loved the idea of Jacob Elordi’s bathwater," she added, referencing a racy scene in "Saltburn." Elsewhere in the interview, Sweeney told the magazine that in spite of her meteoric rise in Hollywood, she doesn’t consider Los Angeles home. SYDNEY SWEENEY CONFESSES SHE WASN’T PREPARED FOR THE EMOTIONAL TOLL OF FAME AMID POLITICAL CONTROVERSIES The 27-year-old "it" girl said she prefers to spend her time at her family’s lake home in Northern Idaho or at her $13.5 million compound with friends in the Florida Keys. "I try not to be here as much as possible," she explained, telling the magazine in the interview that she was planning to head to Idaho for the Fourth of July. Last year, she told Cosmopolitan that most of her friends aren’t in the industry. "I have a really amazing friend group where there are a few who are in this industry, but most of them are not," she said last summer. "You get to step out of what I call ‘the bubble,’ and you see what’s important in life. You see reality, and it grounds and humbles you." She also said in that interview that she and her friends were spending time at the Idaho lake house in between projects. "Most of my friends are still my childhood friends, and that’s why most of them aren’t in the industry, because I didn’t grow up in it," she told Cosmopolitan. "It’s very much just going back to my roots." LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Sweeney convinced her parents to move to Los Angeles when she was 13, after she had started booking acting parts in the Pacific Northwest. She told Travel + Leisure last year, "I go home all the time. What’s so beautiful about the Pacific Northwest is everything that you can do outdoors. . . . There are so many mountains and lakes." Sweeney remembered going berry picking there as a child. "If you go a little bit north of Spokane, [Washington], right next to the border, there’s like all these hidden little waterfalls." Even though she may long for days on the water, Sweeney has made a name for herself as a bit of a workaholic. She’s familiar in both TV and film with shows like "Euphoria" and "The White Lotus" and movies that span horror, rom-com and action, such as "Anyone But You" and "Immaculate." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER "It’s great to do what you love," she told the Journal, "because if you love it, then it doesn’t feel like work, and you want to do it every single day, all the time." She admitted that her nonstop schedule is the way she wants it. After all, she didn’t become one of Hollywood’s most talked-about celebrities by floating on an inner tube. She told the Journal she keeps a busy work schedule "because I don’t want to take six months off. I get anxiety thinking about just taking a few days off." CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP "Being on set is my happy place," she added.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney says 'a lot of Chick-fil-A' and milkshakes fueled dramatic transformation for boxer role
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney gained over 30 pounds on a diet of Chick-fil-A and milkshakes and trained three times daily to portray legendary boxer Christy Martin in the new film "Christy."
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney shared some of the secrets behind her dramatic transformation for her role as legendary boxer Christy Martin in the new movie "Christy." During a Q&A session after the film's premiere at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) on Friday, the 27-year-old actress, who gained more than 30 pounds to play Martin, detailed how her preparations included intense physical training and a diet heavy on Chick-fil-A and milkshakes. "I trained for two or three months before [filming]. I had a boxing coach," she said in a video shared on social media. "I had weight trainers, I had nutritionists. I trained three times a day, every day. And then while I was filming, I trained as well." "And there was a lot of Chick-fil-A," director David Michôd added. SYDNEY SWEENEY IS UNRECOGNIZABLE AS SHE CHANNELS FAMOUS ATHLETE FOR UPCOMING ROLE "A lot of Chick-fil-A, a lot," Sweeney agreed. "A lot of Smucker's, a lot of milkshakes, a lot of protein shakes." "But it was incredible being able to completely embody such a powerful woman," she added. "I felt even stronger. It was truly inspiring." "Christy" tells the story of Martin, nicknamed the "Coal Miner’s Daughter," and her rise from small-town West Virginia to becoming one of the most recognizable female boxers of the 1990s. The film also explores Martin’s troubled relationship with her boxing trainer and husband, Jim Martin (Ben Foster). Their marriage involved codependency, drug abuse, financial scandal, and physical and psychological violence. Martin's tale is also one of survival as she narrowly escaped with her life after Jim attempted to murder her in 2010. Sweeney previously shared that she spent time with Martin, who visited her on set and encouraged her during fight scenes. While standing next to Martin onstage at the Princess of Wales Theatre on Friday, Sweeney teared up as she reflected on playing the former champion. "Thank you for helping us spread Christy's story and awareness, because as you can tell, she is such a special and incredible human being," Sweeney said, drawing cheers and applause from the festival crowd. "Her story deserves to be told." "You're so inspirational, so being able to have her by my side during this process was a dream," the "Euphoria" star told Martin as she became emotional. "But then also just scary, too, because you're like, 'Oh my gosh, we're doing this in front of her,' and I wasn't quite sure." "I mean, she's the greatest boxer in the entire world, and I'm having to do hooks and hits, and I'm like, 'I hope I'm doing this right,'" she added. "It was a dream come true as an actor, as a person." When Martin spoke at the Q&A, she praised Sweeney for capturing both sides of her personality. "Christy the boxer was just the persona, very bombastic and very egotistical, but that is not who I am," Martin explained, according to The Hollywood Reporter. "I am actually very shy and reserved." LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I have these two different parts of my personality, which I think is why Sydney Sweeney does this awesome job," she continued. "She got to be this totally different person that none of you expected. She wasn’t the beautiful, sexy Sydney. She was the tough, rugged Christy in this movie." After her ex-husband's attempt on her life, Martin became a motivational speaker and founded the nonprofit Christy's Champs, which supports domestic violence survivors. Martin told the crowd she hoped her story would inspire others and that the film would give them confidence to pursue their dreams. "I made a deal with God from the hospital: if you let me live, I would help as many people as possible," Martin said of her recovery after the attack. "I hope this movie does that. If a coal miner’s daughter from a 500-person town in southern West Virginia can make it, anybody can." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER According to The Hollywood Reporter, "Christy" received a standing ovation after its premiere. Sweeney's performance has been hailed by critics and "landed immediate Oscar buzz," according to The Associated Press. Ahead of TIFF, Sweeney said she would not be commenting on controversy over her American Eagle "Great Jeans" campaign. Her TIFF appearance marked her first public outing since the ad campaign drew backlash following its July release. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP In an interview with Vanity Fair published earlier this week, Sweeney said she would shut down any questions about the campaign. "I am there to support my movie and the people involved in making it. I’m not there to talk about jeans," the "White Lotus" star said. "The movie’s about Christy, and that’s what I’ll be there to talk about."

articles.title: Show do BTS em SP mostra força coletiva do grupo e tem gritos a favor de Lula e contra Flávio | G1
articles.standfirst: Volta do septeto de K-pop ao Brasil após sete anos teve devoção que fez Morumbis tremer nesta quarta-feira (28). Grupo respondeu com frases em português como ‘Cês não tão de brincadeira’.
articles.summary: Volta do septeto de K-pop ao Brasil após sete anos teve devoção que fez Morumbis tremer nesta quarta-feira (28). Grupo respondeu com frases em português como ‘Cês não tão de brincadeira’.
articles.body:
BTS durante show no MorumBIS, em São Paulo — Foto: Reprodução/X

Em sua quarta vinda ao Brasil, sem contar encontros com fãs e shows solo, o septeto sul-coreano BTS lotou o Morumbis, em São Paulo, nesta quarta-feira (28). Foi um show para matar a saudade do grupo após a turnê anterior, de 2019, que passou por aqui.

Antes do começo e nos poucos silêncios durante o show, fãs puxaram coros politizados como “olê olê olê olá, Lula Lula”, celebrando o presidente, e outros contra Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato derrotado na eleição presidencial que fugiu para os Estados Unidos.

A manifestação política dos fãs tem contexto. Nas últimas semanas, seguidores do BTS fizeram parte de uma mobilização dos fã-clubes no Brasil. Um momento-chave dessa participação ocorreu no domingo seguinte ao primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais, quando o presidente Lula iniciou seu discurso na “Marcha pela Democracia”, em São Paulo, agradecendo a iniciativa dos "fandoms do Brasil".

O protesto nas ruas, realizado em 11 de outubro, foi o resultado de uma organização intensa nas redes sociais, utilizando estratégias típicas dessas comunidades, como mutirões e campanhas com hashtags. Representantes de cerca de 600 fã-clubes, incluindo os de grupos do K-pop, se uniram a favor da candidatura de Lula.

Após o fim do serviço militar e a pausa nos projetos próprios, fica nítido que a ideia agora é mostrar o BTS novamente reunido, sem espaço para performances solo de RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V e Jung Kook.

Os destaques individuais aparecem em uma apresentação com foco no coletivo. RM, Suga e J-Hope dominam os versos com influência do hip hop. Jin, Jimin, V e Jung Kook conduzem a linha vocal mais melodiosa, com momentos dignos de cantores influenciados por soul music.

Também são responsáveis pelos ad-libs, sons curtos que parecem improvisados (às vezes, de fato, são). É um pouco difícil entender toda a dinâmica das versões ao vivo, engolidas pela cantoria em altos decibéis do fandom em faixas como “Fake Love”, da fase “Love Yourself”. Nada supera, no entanto, os hits “Butter” e “Dynamite”, mais perto do fim. Todas elas vêm em versão com sons gravados e vocais, sem a presença de músicos.

As brincadeiras entre os membros dão charme ao show e são motivo de muitos gritos dos fãs. Qualquer momento de interação que pareça fugir do protocolo é recebido com alvoroço, tamanha é a devoção do ARMY, nome da base de fãs do BTS. Nas músicas mais animadas, é possível sentir o estádio tremer.

Em São Paulo, os fãs assistiram aos shows em quatro telões de LED integrados, em vez dos seis usados em outros países. A produtora atribuiu a mudança às limitações logísticas da parte latino-americana da turnê.

O palco 360 graus e as quatro passarelas incrustadas na plateia compensaram a estrutura mais enxuta. Um ponto negativo é a parte em que dançarinos se movimentam com panos, coreografia que remete ao desfile das delegações na abertura das Olimpíadas e pouco acrescenta visualmente. Quando retornam com bastões luminosos, o efeito cênico é bem mais embasbacante.

A plateia chegou cedo e dominou as ruas dos arredores do estádio desde a tarde. A partir das 20h, dominou o estádio com trajes em tons de roxo e acessórios como light sticks, leques e cartazes, muitos com juras de amor em coreano.

Ao vivo, o som da banda é um pouco mais pesado do que nas gravações originais. O k-pop do BTS tem muito do hip hop americano dos anos 1990 e do EDM, a música eletrônica comercial com pegada bem anos 2000. O rap com um quê de pop dançante e o refrão cantarolável estão no DNA da maior parte do repertório. Das novidades, “Body to body” é imbatível, com jeitão de pop rock de arena.

Como boy bands ocidentais (Backstreet Boys e One Direction, por exemplo), o BTS alcança seus melhores resultados como ato pop quando une o talento e o carisma de seus integrantes, com direito a frases em português como “Vocês encheram este estádio gigante” e “Cês não tão de brincadeira”. Quem vai em um show de boyband quer ver coreografias bem sincronizadas, ouvir boas harmonias vocais e se deleitar com frases simpáticas.

Mas diferentemente dos grupos pop estourados nos anos 90, os sete membros não são apenas garotos que cantam e dançam. Das 20 músicas mais ouvidas do BTS no Spotify, 14 têm pelo menos o nome de um integrante entre os compositores.

Anunciada em janeiro, a turnê do álbum “Arirang”, lançado em março de 2026, começou em 9 de abril, em Goyang, na Coreia do Sul.

A agenda segue até março de 2027, com shows na Ásia, América do Norte, Europa, América Latina e Oceania. No Brasil, o BTS se apresenta em três noites no MorumBIS. Além desta quarta, cantam na sexta (30) e no sábado (31) sempre com ingressos esgotados.

articles.title: Joyce Moreno doma o ritmo da 'hard bossa' no álbum 'Never too soon' | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista recai na 'swingueira' com frescor em disco editado por gravadora inglesa com duas faixas em inglês e homenagem ao guitarrista Toninho Horta.
articles.summary: Artista recai na 'swingueira' com frescor em disco editado por gravadora inglesa com duas faixas em inglês e homenagem ao guitarrista Toninho Horta.
articles.body:
Joyce Moreno lança o álbum 'Never too soon' na sexta-feira, 30 de outubro, com nove faixas produzidas pela artista com Tutty Moreno — Foto: Elisa Maciel / Divulgação

♬ “É, respira fundo, meu bem / Segura o samba / ... / E, no mais, estamos aí / Quem sabe a febre tem cura?”, projeta Joyce Moreno em versos do samba “Respira fundo”, uma das nove músicas de “Never too soon”, o álbum que a cantora, compositora e excepcional violonista carioca lançará na sexta-feira, 30 de outubro.

Após a autora fazer prognósticos sombrios na letra, o samba se abre após os dois minutos iniciais e deixa entrar o sol da esperança no futuro e na vida, simbolizado pelas vozes do coro formado pela filha da artista, Ana Martins, com os netos de Joyce, Miguel Martins e Tom Andrade.

Ao lado de “Não à toa”, afro-samba que abre o disco em tons graves, o samba “Respira fundo” sobressai na safra essencialmente inédita e autoral do álbum “Never too soon”.

Editado também em LP e CD, o álbum “Never too soon” é mais um coeso título da discografia lançada por Joyce Moreno pela gravadora inglesa Far Out Recordings, em parceria iniciada há 27 anos com a edição do álbum “Hard bossa” em 1999.

Em “Never too soon”, disco gravado no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) com produção musical orquestrada pela própria Joyce Moreno com o baterista Tutty Moreno, parceiro de vida e música, a artista recai na swingueira com frescor.

Tudo soa novo de novo, ainda que um samba-jazz como “Chovendo na Horta (For my brother Toninho)” – composto por Joyce sem letra em homenagem ao compositor e guitarrista mineiro Toninho Horta, que toca na faixa – possa figurar em qualquer disco lançado por Joyce Moreno nos últimos 30 anos.

Aliás, é sintomático que o repertório de “Never too soon” inclua regravação de “Aldeia de Ogum”, música lançada por Joyce no emblemático álbum “Feminina” (1980) e reprocessada por DJs nas pistas europeias dos anos 1990, em movimento que abriu as portas do mercado europeu para a artista brasileira, vítima de boicote das gravadoras brasileiras na maior parte década de 1980 por ter enfrentado poderosos chefões da indústria do disco.

“Aldeia de Ogum” reaparece no álbum “Never too soon” bafejada pelos sopros orquestrados por Nailor Proveta, clarinetista que também arranjou os metais da aliciante abordagem de “Beija-me” (Roberto Martins e Mário Rossi, 1943), samba lançado há 83 anos na voz do cantor Cyro Monteiro (1913 – 1973), um dos reis do balanço nacional.

A regravação de “Beija-me” faz sentido porque, em essência, “Never too soon” é um disco de balanço, de groove . O ritmo pode vir mais calmo – como na quase melancólica “Saudade”, tema ambientado em atmosfera evocativa da bossa nova e cuja letra se resume à repetição do verso-título “Saudade”, palavra existente somente na língua portuguesa – ou quase sempre mais frenético, como no afro-samba-jazz que dá título ao álbum, “Never too soon”, cantado em inglês, idioma bissexto na discografia de Joyce Moreno. Em qualquer andamento, a artista se mostra senhora do ritmo.

Domadora do ritmo no toque do violão que encantava mestres como Antonio Carlos Jobim (1927 – 1994), Joyce se afina como cantora e instrumentista em total sintonia com a banda-base do álbum, formada pela artista com Tutty Moreno (bateria em todas as faixas e percussão em “Luanda”, tema sem letra, levado pela cantora nos vocalizes), Jorge Helder (baixo acústico e baixo elétrico), Lula Galvão (violão e guitarra) e Marcos Nimrichter (Fender Rhodes e teclados).

Quando chega ao fim com “4:08”, canção composta em inglês e pontuada na gravação pelo sopro do trompete de José Arimatéa, o álbum “Never too soon” reitera que a hard bossa de Joyce Moreno continua nova porque a artista sabe segurar o samba-jazz em qualquer conjuntura musical e social.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere: polícia dos EUA conclui que morte da atriz foi acidental | G1
articles.standfirst: Atriz de "Nashville" e "Heroes" faleceu aos 36 anos em agosto. Laudo final médico apontou mistura letal de fentanil e outras substâncias.
articles.summary: Atriz de "Nashville" e "Heroes" faleceu aos 36 anos em agosto. Laudo final médico apontou mistura letal de fentanil e outras substâncias.
articles.body:
A morte da atriz Hayden Panettiere foi classificada como "acidental" pela polícia da Carolina do Sul, nos EUA. O resultado das investigações foi divulgado pelas autoridades locais nesta quarta-feira (28).

A atriz Hayden Panettiere, conhecida por seus papéis em séries de TV como "Nashville" e "Heroes", morreu aos 36 anos no dia 16 de agosto .

Segundo a polícia local, o resultado final das investigações teve como base a determinação de um médico legista.

As investigações apontaram que a morte da atriz foi causada pelos efeitos tóxicos de fentanil, Xanax e outras drogas e considerada acidental.

"A causa da morte foi determinada como efeitos tóxicos de fentanil, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, metocarbamol e quetiapina", informou o comunicado oficial.

As equipes de emergência foram acionadas por volta das 13h50 para atender a um chamado de parada cardiorrespiratória em um imóvel alugado por aplicativo, em Greenville, na Carolina do Sul.

Os socorristas realizaram procedimentos de emergência para tentar salvar a vida da atriz, mas o óbito foi declarado às 14h32.

Hayden Panettiere morreu neste domingo (16), aos 36 anos — Foto: REUTERS

Ex-atriz mirim, Panettiere ganhou amplo reconhecimento ao dar voz a Dot, a jovem princesa formiga no sucesso de animação da Pixar de 1998, "Vida de Inseto". Seu trabalho no álbum de leitura conjunta do filme lhe rendeu uma indicação ao Grammy de Melhor Álbum de Palavra Falada para Crianças.

Ela alcançou a fama interpretando Claire Bennet, uma líder de torcida do ensino médio com superpoderes, na série de sucesso da NBC "Heroes", que estreou em 2006. Ela também participou do drama de futebol americano "Duelo de Titãs" (Remember the Titans), de 2000, estrelado por Denzel Washington.

Panettiere recebeu duas indicações ao Globo de Ouro, em 2013 e 2014, na categoria de Melhor Atriz Coadjuvante em Série de Televisão, Minissérie ou Filme para Televisão por seu papel como Juliette Barnes no drama musical "Nashville". Ela também fez parte da franquia de terror "Pânico".

A aparição mais recente de Panettiere foi no thriller psicológico "Sleepwalker", lançado nos EUA em janeiro de 2026, no qual ela interpretou uma mãe enlutada atormentada por episódios de sonambulismo, de acordo com o site IMDb.

Seu irmão, o ator Jansen Panettiere, morreu em 2023, aos 28 anos, devido a complicações relacionadas a um coração dilatado e a um problema na válvula aórtica, de acordo com um comunicado da família divulgado à imprensa americana ainda naquele ano.

Em 2022, a atriz havia revelado em entrevista à revista People um vício em drogas e álcool que quase lhe custou a vida. "Eu estava no topo do mundo e arruinei tudo", disse.

Panettiere contou que passou anos lutando contra o vício, ao mesmo tempo em que enfrentava uma depressão pós-parto. A atriz buscou tratamento para sua depressão, mas se viu cada vez mais dependente do álcool. "Havia apenas essa cor cinza na minha vida", lamentou.

Hayden Panettiere chega à 61ª edição do Primetime Emmy Awards em 20 de setembro de 2009, em Los Angeles — Foto: AP Photo/Matt Sayles, File

A atriz diz que não bebeu durante a gestação, mas afirma: "Nunca tive a sensação de querer prejudicar minha filha, mas não queria passar nenhum tempo com ela."

Panettiere conta que trabalhou bastante para ser sincera consigo mesma para encarar uma internação e um tratamento de trauma no ano passado. "Acho que cheguei ao fundo do poço, mas lá há aquele alçapão que se abre."

Na entrevista, a atriz, que iniciou sua carreira aos 11 anos, atuando em novelas e filmes como "Duelo de Titãs", ainda revelou que, quando ela estava com 15 anos, um membro de sua equipe começou a oferecer "pílulas da felicidade" para que ela caminhasse nos tapetes vermelhos.

"Era pra me deixar animada durante as entrevistas. E não fazia ideia de que aquilo não era apropriado, ou que era a porta de abertura para meu vício", conta.

articles.title: Heidi Klum, Queen of Halloween, drops another hint for this year's 'bloody' costume
articles.summary: Each year, Klum unveils her full costume at her star-studded costume party on Oct. 31 in New York City.
articles.body:
The Queen of Halloween is back! Supermodel Heidi Klum, known for her grotesque, over-the-top Halloween looks, took to Instagram on Wednesday to share another sneak peek of this year's costume.

Klum shared a video of prosthetics that appeared to resemble fungus.

"Have u figured it out yet?? Only time will tell 🤫 3 more days…," Klum captioned the clip.

Fans have continued flooding Klum's comments with guesses, including Monstro Elisasue from The Substance , a Clicker from The Last of Us , Vecna from Stranger Things and a monster from Resident Evil.

Klum's longtime collaborator, special effects makeup artist Mike Marino, previously dropped a hint of his own. While chatting with NBC's Hollywood ReelTime , Marino revealed that Klum's look this year is "one of the most elaborate costumes ever made."

"It's so difficult to do and just the complication of it is really challenging," Marino said. "It might not appear to some people sometimes how much work goes into it but there's so much that goes into these things."

The supermodel shared another hint on Tuesday, with an image of even more prosthetics.

"4 more days," Klum wrote, alongside a series of spooky emoji. "#HeidiHalloween."

Klum initially teased this year's gruesome creation on Oct. 24, sharing a close-up on Instagram.

The mysterious image appears to show an array of prosthetics resembling human organs. Klum's fans were quick to share their predictions for her costume. Guesses ranged from short and sweet to hyper-specific, from "Coral reef. Inspired by St. Barth's" to "pirates of the caribbean when the pirates become sea creatures on the flying dutchman."

"Internal organs?" one commenter asked, while another remarked, "Looks like the inside of a stomach."

"Idk but I'm gagging already," admitted another fan.

Klum has been sparing with her hints. Aside from the graphic, organ-like prosthetics, the supermodel told Parade that this year's costume will be "bloody."

It looks like we'll have to wait a few more days for Klum's final look. Each year, Klum unveils her full costume at her star-studded costume party on Oct. 31 in New York City. This year marks her 25th annual Halloween bash.

When it comes to her costume for All Hallows' Eve, Klum has a history of going all-out . Over the years, Klum has consistently debuted high-concept, unsightly transformations. Her greatest hits include E.T., a gigantic peacock, a slinky worm, a skin-baring zombie creature and Fiona from Shrek . Last year, Klum slithered into her costume bash as Medusa, complete with a scaled body, a tail and a head of snakes. Klum's husband, Tom Kaulitz, is always game to help bring her vision to life too, whether he's dressed as the Greek soldier that Medusa turned to stone, a bloodied fisherman or the Shrek to her Fiona.

Klum opened up about what sparked her desire to throw a costume party every Halloween, telling Parade, "I'd go to some of these Halloween parties and people were just not given anything."

Klum isn't concerned with looking sexy on Halloween. In fact, she prefers to go in the complete opposite direction. After seeing one too many unimpressive costumes, she decided to take matters into her own hands, hosting her first Halloween party in 2000.

"This is really how it sparked my idea on doing one myself because I thought all the parties were so lame and the costumes people were doing even lamer," Klum told Parade. "I was like, 'There needs to be a person who really shows them to give more.'"

articles.title: Hasan Piker files $72.5 million defamation suit against Scott Jennings
articles.summary: The progressive pundit claims the conservative commentator deliberately distorted his remarks to falsely portray him as a supporter of lynching Black people.
articles.body: Progressive pundit Hasan Piker has filed a $72.5 million defamation lawsuit against conservative commentator Scott Jennings, claiming Jennings deliberately distorted his remarks to falsely portray him as a supporter of lynching Black people. Piker, in a 38-page complaint filed Tuesday in federal court in Washington, D.C., said Jennings defamed him on an Aug. 11 episode of “The Scott Jennings Show” when he played video from a 2024 livestream of Piker’s show that had been doctored. “Mr. Jennings did not merely mischaracterize something Mr. Piker said,” the complaint says. “He took a false, fabricated, and manipulated video of Mr. Piker, added a made-up quotation that Mr. Piker never uttered, and then made accusations that went beyond even what the manipulated footage purported to show.” Jennings, who is also a CNN commentator, described Piker on the broadcast as a “radical socialist streamer” and Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s “best friend” who has been “calling for Black voters to be lynched.” “Listen for yourself and understand what the socialists have in store for the black community,” Jennings posted. “Mr. Piker has never advocated the lynching of Black Americans, or anyone else,” the complaint says. “He has never called for a return to lynchings. And he has never proposed anything remotely resembling the supposed plan that Mr. Jennings falsely attributed to him.” Jennings did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In the complaint, Piker’s legal team says it sent a written demand to Jennings’ lawyers in August that they issue a retraction. Jennings’ legal team acknowledged it received the letter and said a response would follow, but no “substantive response” has been issued, the complaint says. As of Wednesday, Jennings’ post including the disputed video was still on X and had racked up 3 million views. Piker’s legal team also suggests in the complaint that in addition to undermining El-Sayed’s support among Black voters in Michigan, Jennings had a “professional and political incentive” to smear Piker. “In the weeks surrounding the publications, Mr. Jennings was publicly reported to be under consideration for the position of White House Press Secretary,” the complaint says. Piker, who is seeking $27.5 million in compensatory damages and $45 million in punitive damages, is a social media maven with more than 3.1 million Twitch followers, 2 million YouTube subscribers and roughly 1.9 million followers on Instagram. While Piker has campaigned on behalf of several Democratic candidates, he remains a controversial figure in the party, and several Jewish organizations have accused him of promoting antisemitic tropes and downplaying the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attack on Israel. In the complaint, Piker alleges that the video Jennings aired combined video from three separate Twitch livestreams and rearranged the sequence of his remarks. Also, it says, the video shows Piker making sarcastic remarks about going back “to a better time when lynchings were happening.” But the makers of the video edited out the Oct. 29, 2024, YouTube debate between two Black political commentators — one liberal, the other conservative — that Piker was reacting to. After a clip of the conservative commentator blaming “woke DAs” for policies that harm Black people ran, the complaint says, Piker responded: “He said, ‘We need more Klansmen, okay? Can we go back to a better time when lynchings were happening? This is what I like as a Black man. Also, there’s no real racism in America.’ My man said, ‘woke DAs,’ dude. What are you saying?” That clip was taken out of context and presented on Jennings’ show with the caption “PIKER: ‘LET’S GO BACK TO A BETTER TIME WHEN LYNCHINGS WERE HAPPENING,’” which the complaint says Piker never said. “Mr. Piker was mocking the conservative commentator’s statement,” the complaint says. “Mr. Piker obviously was not expressing support for the Ku Klux Klan, lynching, or racial discrimination.” Daniel Watkins, an attorney for Piker, told NBC News that what Jennings presented was “a lie.” “There is something especially disgraceful about exploiting this country’s history of racial terror to destroy another man’s reputation,” Watkins said. “Scott Jennings has every right to disagree with Hasan Piker. He has no right to invent what Hasan said.”

articles.title: Jorge de Juan anuncia que padece un cáncer de páncreas en estadio IV que no se puede operar: "No sé cuánto tiempo me queda"
articles.standfirst: El actor, que ha participado en películas como 'Abre los ojos' o 'Las bicicletas son para el verano', ha desvelado su delicado estado de salud en su cuenta de Instagram
articles.summary: El actor, que ha participado en películas como 'Abre los ojos' o 'Las bicicletas son para el verano', ha desvelado su delicado estado de salud en su cuenta de Instagram
articles.body: El actor Jorge de Juan ha anunciado que padece un cáncer de páncreas en estadio IV que no se puede operar ni resecar. El intérprete, con una extensa trayectoria en cine, televisión y teatro, ha compartido la noticia a través de su cuenta de Instagram para aclarar las informaciones que circulaban sobre su estado de salud y responder a las preguntas de amigos y seguidores. "No me gusta hablar de mí en redes sociales. Pero hay amigos y amigas por ahí preguntando y algunos diciendo cosas que no son ciertas. Para que quede claro: llevo muchos meses con problemas digestivos y abdominales que han derivado en un cáncer de páncreas en estadio IV, que no se puede operar ni resecar", ha escrito el también director y productor teatral. Jorge de Juan ha explicado que, en su situación actual, el objetivo del tratamiento es intentar frenar la expansión del cáncer, a la espera de que la ciencia encuentre una solución. "Yo creo en los milagros y, como creyente que soy, tengo fe en que voy a sanar si la ciencia no encuentra una respuesta", ha añadido. En su mensaje, Jorge de Juan también ha reconocido la incertidumbre que afronta ante la enfermedad. "No sé cuánto tiempo me queda. Espero que mucho", ha señalado, antes de agradecer el apoyo y el cariño que está recibiendo. "Estoy seguro de que vuestro apoyo, vuestros mensajes, vuestras velas y, sobre todo, vuestro cariño me darán fuerzas para afrontar esta nueva aventura que he emprendido con una sonrisa como mejor arma para vivirla", ha concluido. A lo largo de su carrera, Jorge de Juan ha participado en más de 30 películas y series de televisión. Entre sus trabajos cinematográficos figuran títulos como 'Abre los ojos', 'Las bicicletas son para el verano', 'Beltenebros', 'Silencio en la nieve', 'Talk of Angels' ('Pasiones rotas'), 'One of the Hollywood Ten' ('Punto de mira') y 'Agente contrainteligente’, además de su participación en la película 'La Palma’. Nacido en Cartagena el 6 de junio de 1961, la trayectoria de Jorge de Juan también está estrechamente ligada al teatro, donde ha intervenido en más de 20 producciones. Entre las obras en las que ha participado destacan 'Bodas de sangre', 'Calígula', 'Edipo Rey', 'Macbeth', 'Ricardo III', 'Los 39 escalones', 'La mujer de negro' y 'Hay que deshacer la casa'. Además de su trabajo como actor, ha desarrollado una carrera como director y productor teatral, con montajes como 'El público', 'Al final del arco iris', 'Drácula', 'La casa de Bernarda Alba' y 'Yerma', representados tanto en España como en el Reino Unido. En 2016, Jorge de Juan fundó el Cervantes Theatre de Londres, el primer teatro de habla hispana en la historia del teatro británico, que se convirtió en sede de la Spanish Theatre Company, de la que fue director hasta su cierre en 2025.

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes' most famous photo started with a simple request from a photographer
articles.summary: Photographer Ethan Pines looks back on shooting the now iconic photo of Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in 2014.
articles.body:
Ethan Pines shot Elizabeth Holmes for a Forbes cover story in 2014.

The photo of Holmes holding a blood vial has become synonymous with the disgraced Theranos founder.

Pines spoke to Business Insider about meeting Holmes and his thoughts on "You Can See Everything."

As photographer Ethan Pines drove to the Theranos offices in Silicon Valley, all he could think about was how to make his shoot with its founder, Elizabeth Holmes , stand out.

It was 2014, and the hype around Holmes' health technology company, which boasted it could run hundreds of medical and diagnostic tests using only a few drops of blood, had hit its zenith. The 30-year-old Holmes was on the verge of becoming the youngest self-made female billionaire with a net worth of $4.5 billion.

Pines had photographed CEOs before, and he was racking his brain for ways to make the visuals for Holmes' Forbes cover story memorable.

He never could have predicted that his shot of Holmes would become the symbol of the now-disgraced CEO's meteoric rise and spectacular fall, not to mention imitated on TV series , put on billboards , and discussed in a popular documentary.

Twelve years later, Pines' photo of Holmes has re-entered the zeitgeist thanks to Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's hit documentary, "You Can See Everything," which chronicles the life of Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, in the final weeks before Holmes reports to prison for defrauding investors.

Pines' famous shot is brought up several times in the doc. At one point, while having her body scanned to create an AI hologram, Holmes breaks down, recalling how her image has become a symbol of duplicity in the press.

This isn't the first time Pines' photo of Holmes has gone viral. The shot was used on the poster for Alex Gibney's 2019 documentary on Holmes , "The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley." The shot is also re-created in the 2022 Hulu miniseries "The Dropout," which stars Amanda Seyfried as Holmes. But Pines said "You Can See Everything" has brought an even larger wave attention to his work.

"I posted on my Instagram the entire shoot in a flipbook motion piece, and it has a million views," Pines said. "My posts don't get anywhere near that."

When Pines arrived on set that day in 2014, he knew he wanted to take photographs that functioned as both a portrait of a young founder and a showcase of her invention.

"In my mind, I pictured a tight shot with her holding something up," Pines told Business Insider.

Halfway through the shoot, he asked Holmes' team if there was a suitable object they could use. They obliged with a small vial of blood (well, fake blood; the real stuff, he was told, was in a temperature-controlled lab down the hall).

Once Holmes held the vial up to her face, everything clicked into place.

"Sometimes when you're shooting, you're thinking to yourself, 'This is a gift,'" Pines recalled. "With her big eyes and that intimate, interesting expression, I felt we had something."

Unlike the typical photoshoot with a CEO, where Pines would only get around 10 to 20 minutes to photograph his subject before they rushed off to attend to other matters, Holmes was generous with her time.

Over a couple hours, Pines said he took a total of 220 shots — 52 of her holding the blood vial — in three different setups. What stood out to him the most was Holmes' persona. She was relaxed and down to earth, chatting it up with Pines and his assistant. She'd done her own hair and makeup for the shoot.

Pines recognized a similar easy charisma on display in "You Can See Everything."

"I cannot say if she's being real in this movie or putting on a facade to Nathan Fielder, but it reminded me of my experience," he said. "I felt she was really approachable; she's humble, makes a lot of eye contact, and doesn't come across as cocky or uptight. Oblivious to everything going on around her."

With the doc a hit at the box office , Pines doesn't think the Holmes hype will die down anytime soon. He's constantly seeing reminders of his iconic photo.

"I was at a Halloween carnival for my daughter's school, and there were at least two people dressed as Elizabeth Holmes with the little blood vial," he said. "The whole thing is a trip."

"You Can See Everything" is in theaters now.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence Filmed a Nude Scene and Discovered Crew Members Who Were Not Approved to Be on Set: ‘I Came Down Hard on That’
articles.summary: Jennifer Lawrence revealed on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast that she once discovered while filming a nude scene that there were crew members on set who were n...
articles.body:
Jennifer Lawrence revealed on the "Call Her Daddy" podcast that she once discovered while filming a nude scene that there were crew members on set who were not approved to be there during the filming of such intimate material. The incident prompted Lawrence to "come down hard" on the crew and remains one of the definitive moments in her acting career that taught her the importance of speaking out.

When asked if she's gotten more comfortable over the years in advocating for herself, Lawrence responded: "You have to be malleable. That's part of the job. When Lynne Ramsay for 'Die My Love' says cut your hair and get mullet bangs and dye it platinum blonde… that's the gig. You have to be malleable. But I definitely speak up more now because I am aware of the place I have in the industry."

"There was an instance on set where crew members who were not approved when I was doing nudity were on set. I came down hard on it, purely because if we are not setting that principle then what on earth is going to happen to an 18-year-old unknown when she shows up and there's people on set who are not approved to be there? She's going to be in a position of do I say something and get a reputation for being difficult or do I let these people who I'm not comfortable with see me naked. It was important to me to explain that to the people why that was not okay."

Lawrence is no stranger to nudity or sex scenes in her movie. She went viral last year for her comments about forgoing an intimacy coordinator during the filming of "Die My Love" with Robert Pattinson.

"We did not have [an intimacy coordinator], or maybe we did but we didn't really… I felt really safe with Rob," Lawrence said on the "Las Culturistas podcast. "He is not pervy and very in love with [partner] Suki Waterhouse. We mostly were just talking about our kids and relationships. There was never any weird like, 'Does he think I like him?' If there was a little bit of that I would probably have an intimacy coordinator. A lot of male actors get offended if you don't want to fuck them, and then the punishment starts. He was not like that."

As for the movie's nude scenes: "I don't care about nudity. I'm not sensitive about it. I wanted Lynne to have total freedom artistically… I think being pregnant took a lot of, like, vanity anxiety away. Before 'No Hard Feelings,' I was dieting and not eating carbs and working out. I was pregnant [for 'Die My Love']. Like, what was I gonna do? Not eat? I was working 15 hours a day. I was just tired… I remember, like, them sending over a close-up of cellulite and being like, 'Do you want us to touch this up?' And I was like, 'No. That's an ass.'"

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's death ruled accidental by South Carolina police
articles.summary: A South Carolina coroner previously confirmed Panettiere died from an accidental drug overdose that included fentanyl.
articles.body:
The death of Hayden Panettiere has been ruled accidental, South Caroline police announced Wednesday.

Greenville Police Department said the investigation into Panettiere's death has been concluded "based on the Medical Examiner's determination and the findings of the investigation," and the actor's death was officially ruled accidental.

Last month, a South Carolina coroner confirmed Panettiere died from an accidental drug overdose that included fentanyl. There were no signs of trauma, the coroner's office said.

Emergency responders were called to a residence where Panettiere, 36, had been staying in Greenville, South Carolina, on the afternoon of Aug. 16. Despite "advanced cardiac life support measures," she was pronounced dead there, the Greenville County Coroner's Office said.'

Panettiere's on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach were at the scene of her death, according to a police report obtained by CBS News . The Hickersons made the 911 call that brought first responders to the apartment.

Authorities, including the Drug Enforcement Administration, were investigating the circumstances of Panettiere's death. Police previously said that a preliminary investigation "has not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances."

articles.title: Modric says Milan ‘deserved’ defeat against Bologna: ‘We didn’t expect it’
articles.summary: Milan star Luka Modric admits the Rossoneri deserved to lose to Bologna, especially after their second-half performance: ‘We didn’t expect it.’Milan suffered...
articles.body:
Milan star Luka Modric admits the Rossoneri deserved to lose to Bologna, especially after their second-half performance: 'We didn't expect it.'

Milan suffered a 4-2 home loss to Bologna on Wednesday. It was the Rossoneri's first Serie A defeat this season.

"It was a bad defeat; we didn't expect it, especially after the first half," Modric told Sky Sport Italia via Milannews.

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Luka Modric of AC Milan in action during the warm up before the Serie A match between SS Lazio and AC Milan at Stadio Olimpico on September 12, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

"I think we had done well in the league until now, and tonight we lost our first game. We lost so many duels in the second half. That set-piece goal was unfortunate, and from that moment we threw ourselves down. We deserved to lose.

"We have no excuses. There have been injuries, but it's a positive that the next game is right away. We had done really well until tonight, so we must stay optimistic and hope to react on Saturday," he continued.

Modric started on the bench and was introduced during the break to replace the injured Fikayo Tomori .

Milan will face city rivals Inter in their next league game on Saturday.

UDINE, ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Luka Modric of Milan in action during the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on October 25, 2026 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images)

Despite their latest defeat, Modric feels the Rossoneri are heading in the right direction under Ruben Amorim.

"I think we are going the right way. The coach has arrived with new ideas, with a new style of play, and we are trying to understand his ideas and what he asks of us," the midfielder argued.

"As I said before, we had done well until tonight. You can always do more, but we still need to improve, and we hope to do it during the season."

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Samuel Mbangula of Bologna FC 1909 celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammates during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 28, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Milan are now fifth in the Serie A table with 18 points in nine matches. The Rossoneri have won five games, drawn three and lost once.

Modric, 41, is under contract with Milan until the end of the season. He has provided two assists in nine Serie A games so far this season.

articles.title: De Rossi joy at beating mentor Spalletti: ‘Genoa showed heart and spirit’
articles.summary: Daniele De Rossi admits it ‘means a lot’ for him to beat mentor Luciano Spalletti, as Genoa swept Juventus aside 2-0. ‘The team showed heart and spirit.’The...
articles.body:
Daniele De Rossi admits it 'means a lot' for him to beat mentor Luciano Spalletti, as Genoa swept Juventus aside 2-0. 'The team showed heart and spirit.'

The two coaches took the unusual step of having their pre-match interview together on live television, confirming the strong rapport they had when De Rossi was Luciano Spalletti's player at Roma.

Now the student has become the master, beating his mentor 2-0 with goals from Kingsley Ehizibue and Tommaso Baldanzi in the first half.

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Daniele De Rossi, head coach of Genoa, looks on during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Juventus FC at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

"It was a complete performance, because we held out under pressure a lot better than we had done in recent matches," De Rossi told DAZN Italia.

"It was a pretty difficult fixture for us, but the team showed heart and spirit, also with a few good attacking moves, so we are really happy."

Genoa have now registered three consecutive home victories after beating Venezia and Fiorentina, but seeing off Juventus is a huge confidence booster going forward.

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Luciano Spalletti, head coach of Juventus, reacts during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Juventus FC at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

"I started thinking about coaching very early, already from the age of 25 or 26," revealed De Rossi.

"The older I got, the more I thought about my second career. Now I am taking on those giants of the profession, and it means a lot to me having won against coaches like Spalletti and Gian Piero Gasperini.

"However, the difference this evening was made by the players."

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Tommaso Baldanzi of Genoa (4th from left) scores a goal during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Juventus FC at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Baldanzi had struggled for regular playing time, but he was decisive this even and scored the second goal too.

"We evaluated his characteristics, he hadn't had much space lately and I wanted to play him at all costs, because he was in good shape. We took him to the other side to where he usually plays, so we could isolate Lucumi in the Juve defence.

"Now that the referees allow more challenges and don't give as many fouls, playing the ball to feet becomes counter-productive, so we've got to get into those spaces instead.

"All the players were marvellous tonight, we made five or six changes and will make more against Lecce."

articles.title: Empreendedora cria escola de ourivesaria e vê joia desfilar no Oscar | G1
articles.standfirst: Além da marca própria, empresária comanda uma escola de ourivesaria que já revelou novos talentos e empreendedores do setor.
articles.summary: Negócio nasceu após o fechamento da antiga escola onde ela lecionava e hoje reúne ensino, produção e vendas de joias.
articles.body:
Uma joia criada em São Paulo ganhou projeção internacional ao integrar o visual da atriz Alice Carvalho no Oscar de 2026.

Por trás da peça está a ourives e empreendedora Luiza Simões, que transformou a paixão pela joalheria em um ecossistema de negócios que reúne marca própria, loja física e uma escola dedicada à formação de novos profissionais do setor.

A trajetória de Luiza começou em um ateliê de ourivesaria, onde aprendeu técnicas como serrar, soldar e modelar metais. Após concluir o curso, ela foi convidada para dar aulas no mesmo espaço. Quando a escola encerrou as atividades, a empreendedora viu a carreira tomar um rumo inesperado.

“Foi um pouco desesperador no início, mas foi o começo de muita coisa nova. Eu nem sabia que isso ia acontecer e, de repente, foi um novo momento”, relembra.

Determinada a continuar ensinando, Luiza alugou uma sala na mesma rua e começou a estruturar a própria escola. Sem investidores externos, contou com a ajuda dos próprios alunos, que adiantaram o pagamento das aulas para viabilizar a compra dos primeiros equipamentos.

Hoje, a escola funciona há três anos e já recebeu cerca de 100 alunos . O curso é dividido em três módulos, com carga horária total de 30 horas e investimento de R$ 4.890 .

Joia usada no Oscar coloca empreendedora brasileira no radar internacional — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

O público é variado, reunindo desde jovens interessados em aprender uma nova profissão até pessoas em busca de recolocação ou especialização. Segundo Luiza, muitos ex-alunos seguiram carreira no setor e criaram as próprias marcas.

Um exemplo é Catarina Salles, que começou a estudar ourivesaria aos 17 anos e, aos 19, já mantém uma marca própria no mesmo endereço da escola. Ela afirma que o aprendizado proporcionou autonomia técnica para desenvolver as próprias criações.

Além da escola, Luiza administra sua marca de joias, que vende peças na loja física e pela internet . Com formação inicial em artes cênicas, ela aposta no audiovisual para apresentar as coleções e construir narrativas em torno dos produtos.

“A gente trouxe uma linguagem de cinema que foi bem importante para conseguir vender o nosso produto e dizer o que ele é. Porque não é só uma joia, tem muita narrativa por trás”, afirma.

A estratégia ajudou a ampliar o alcance da marca. Em 2025, a empreendedora participou de eventos de joalheria e moda em Milão e Paris. No ano seguinte, uma de suas criações chegou ao Oscar : o broche ByaYala, usado por Alice Carvalho no tapete vermelho da premiação.

A peça faz referência a um termo de origem do povo Kuna, associado à América Latina. “Quando a gente foi chamado para fazer o Oscar, eu senti que muito da minha trajetória estava atingindo um objetivo”, conta.

Com uma equipe de quatro professores na escola e projetos em andamento nos Estados Unidos, Europa e Japão, Luiza afirma que o reconhecimento internacional representa apenas uma etapa da caminhada.

"É só o início ainda. Tem muita coisa para vir pela frente. Novos desafios vêm que a gente nem imaginava como lidar. E é aí que vem o lugar do empreendedor: tem que inventar”, diz.

articles.title: Lost Frequencies wants a Bollywood collab: ‘I’d love to do some Bollywood-style sessions!
articles.summary: Belgian DJ Lost Frequencies expresses his desire to collaborate with Bollywood artists, sharing insights on Indian music's influence in electronic genres and his love for performing in India.
articles.body: Belgian DJ and music producer Felix De Laet, better known by his stage name Lost Frequencies, is keen to explore Bollywood music and collaborate with Indian artists. Having performed in India several times over the years, the artiste says he is fascinated by the way Indian music is finding its way into electronic music sets and productions.“I think it’s super interesting and I’m always intrigued to see how other artists interpret Bollywood and native Indian music into their sets or tracks. I do want to work with more Indian artists and would really like to do some Bollywood-style sessions! I recently did a Kesariya remix and worked on some edits that I played at the show,” he says.The DJ, who performed at Casa Bacardi Mountain Edition in Dehradun, says India's vibrant culture and audiences continue to draw him back. “I love playing in India, the culture over in this part of the world is so bright, colourful and I always feel a real natural kinship and bright energy when I perform. As my visits have grown across India over the years, I am always so proud to be supported by such a beautiful country and its people; the Indian music scene is also very diverse when listeners or fellow artists scratch beneath the surface and that is exciting to me,” he says.On performing against a mountain backdrop, he adds, “I feel like I can really tap into another side of energy in such a beautiful setting and audiences want music to match that, something I hope to bring to them with a mixture of classics and feel-good vibes — and lots of new music to make the show special!”Known for blending emotive melodies with dance-floor-friendly beats, Lost Frequencies says his creative process can begin with anything from a lyric to a melody or rhythm. “For me it can come from a range of places, sometimes a lyric when working with a songwriter or vocalist and then I will build a certain production around that, sometimes it is the other way around, focusing in on a specific vibe through a melody or rhythm. Sometimes that is more upbeat in the electronic world, sometimes it is more melancholy or pop-leaning, but I always want to bring a signature Lost Frequencies sound to everything I make. Feel-good and from the heart!”While technology and social media continue to change the electronic music landscape, he is optimistic about what younger artistes will bring to the genre. “I’m always excited to see new developments in the industry. Of course, many people share the passion of music as fans, artists, producers and people behind the scenes in all making this crazy industry tick along! But I think the fact that technology is constantly evolving and fresh ideas are being explored, that will always be a positive aspect to look forward to with what will come next and newer generations,” he says.Despite spending much of the year travelling for performances, the DJ reveals that he enjoys the quieter side of life, too. “That really I am a homebody! I travel so much with hundreds of shows a year, and for that I am so thankful for all my fans at my shows and festival appearances, there really is no feeling like that and being able to create and perform my music is still my dream come true. I appreciate the fun and travelling of being on tour which in turn also makes me appreciate the little things back in Belgium more, it’s a nice mix to have.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor reunites with 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' co-star Poorna Jagannathan at 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' LA premiere; actress encourages fans to watch epic in 3D
articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor reunited with his 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' co-star Poorna Jagannathan at the Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'.
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor reunited with his 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' co-star Poorna Jagannathan at the Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'. The actress, who played Riana Sarai in the 2013 romantic drama directed by Ayan Mukerji, shared a picture with Ranbir on her social media handle, giving fans a glimpse of their reunion backstage, more than a decade after their film together.Poorna, posted the picture on Instagram, posing alongside Ranbir, who essays the role of Kabir 'Bunny' Thapar in the film. The photograph from the premiere has since caught the attention of fans, who were delighted to see the two actors together again. She also added the song 'Ilahi' sung by Mohit Chauhan, to the post.She also shared a photo from inside the theatre and posed for a photo in front of the film's poster that featured on the big screen.Poorna made headlines last year, when she got candid about facing ageism in Bollywood. The actress, who starred in Abhinay Deo's 2011 film 'Delhi Belly', said she found it difficult to get roles. "I did 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' but I just felt underestimated. There was just no role for me. There was intense ageism in the industry when I was there. Things have really shifted. Priyanka, Deepika and all these people are really shifting what it means to be a woman in their forties, but not when I was there. I felt like I would've loved to have worked more, but it just didn't happen."The Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' took place at the David Geffen Theatre inside the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 27. The special screening was attended by the film's lead cast, including Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, along with director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra. Several international celebrities, including Jada Pinkett Smith, attended the screening.Ranbir plays Lord Rama in the ambitious two-part epic, with Sai Pallavi portraying Sita and Yash taking on the villainous role of Ravana. articles.title: Bhumi Pednekar to reunite with Akshay Kumar after four years; actress joins Priyadarshan's upcoming film: Reports
articles.summary: Bhumi Pednekar is reportedly returning to the big screen and she will reunite with Akshay Kumar in an upcoming film directed by Priyadarshan.
articles.body: Bhumi Pednekar is reportedly returning to the big screen and she will reunite with Akshay Kumar in an upcoming film directed by Priyadarshan.As per the latest reports, Priyadarshan has confirmed Bhumi's casting as the female lead in the project. The film will reunite Akshay and Bhumi, four years after their last release together, 'Raksha Bandhan', states a report on HT City. Although details about the upcoming movie remain limited, the reunion adds another collaboration to the actors' shared filmography.Akshay Kumar and Bhumi Pednekar's previous filmsAkshay Kumar and Bhumi Pednekar first worked together in 'Toilet: Ek Prem Katha', released in 2017. Directed by Shree Narayan Singh, the social drama explored sanitation and open defecation in India. The film used a relationship at its centre to address a wider social issue.The actors later reunited for 'Raksha Bandhan', which arrived in theatres in 2022. Directed by Aanand L Rai, the family comedy-drama followed a brother who wanted to arrange marriages for his sisters. Akshay played the brother, while Bhumi portrayed his childhood sweetheart. Their next project with Priyadarshan would therefore be their third film together. It would also end a four-year gap since audiences last saw them share the screen in 'Raksha Bandhan'.Bhumi Pednekar received praise for 'Daldal'Bhumi Pednekar has continued to explore different roles in recent years. Earlier this year, she received appreciation for her performance in the series 'Daldal'. The actress' last film to arrive in cinemas was 'Mere Husband Ki Biwi'. The romantic comedy premiered on February 21, 2025.Actress visits Shirdi, Ujjain and TirupatiAway from her acting commitments, Bhumi Pednekar recently undertook a spiritual journey that included visits to several religious destinations. She began the pilgrimage in Shirdi, Maharashtra, before travelling to the Mahakaleshwar Temple in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. Her itinerary also included Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh.
